title: Coaching 1:1 Playbook and Performance Mapping
author: Sophie Tran
content:
Summary:
This playbook provides a practical, repeatable framework for managers to run regular 1:1s, perform structured performance mapping, and drive consistent development outcomes across teams. It combines a reusable 1:1 agenda, coaching prompts, a performance mapping matrix, probation/90-day checklists, calibration meeting guidance, and lightweight templates for written feedback. The goal is to reduce variance in manager coaching quality and create defensible records for growth and promotion conversations.

Who this is for:
- Frontline managers across engineering, product, and support
- People Ops partners and HRBP reviewers
- People managers new to Redwood or switching teams

Owner and SLAs:
- Playbook owner: People Ops (Sophie Tran)
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review or after major org changes
- Adoption SLO: 95% of managers run documented 1:1s at least twice/month for direct reports within 3 months of rollout

1) 1:1 Cadence and Format
- Frequency: recommended weekly for ICs in active projects; bi-weekly acceptable for senior ICs or low-touch roles.
- Minimum expectation: every direct report should have at least 20 documented 1:1s per year.
- Length: 30–45 minutes for ICs; 45–60 minutes for managers and senior ICs.
- Mode: in-person preferred when onboarding or discussing promotion; remote OK with videocall and notes shared.

Standard 1:1 agenda (use as a template):
- 2 mins: Quick personal check-in (energy, context)
- 5 mins: Wins since last meeting (celebrate progress)
- 10 mins: Roadblocks & support needed (clear asks and owners)
- 10 mins: Development focus (skills, stretch projects, feedback)
- 5 mins: Career conversation or long-term goals (rotate monthly)
- 3 mins: Commitments & next steps (owner + due date)

Note template for managers (one-line entries encouraged):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD | Focus: [project|development|blocker|career] | Summary: 1-2 lines | Action items: owner (due)

2) Coaching Prompts and Feedback Frameworks
- Goal of coaching: increase capability and autonomy; reduce ambiguity for the report.
- Use 'RAD' shorthand for feedback:
  - Recognize: what worked?
  - Adjust: what to change?
  - Develop: growth action for next 4–8 weeks
- When delivering corrective feedback, use structured observation + impact + request pattern:
  1. Observable fact (what happened)
  2. Impact (on team, customer, delivery)
  3. Clear request (what change you want to see, timeline)

3) Performance Mapping Matrix (one-page view)
- Purpose: translate ongoing 1:1 evidence into a consistent rubric for development conversations and promotion calibration.
- Matrix axes and guidance (manager fill-in per report):
  - X-axis: Results (consistently delivers to expectations -> exceeds expectations)
  - Y-axis: Behaviors & Collaboration (needs support -> role-model)
- Quadrant actions:
  - Q1 (Low results / Low behaviors): immediate development plan + 30/60/90 checkpoints
  - Q2 (Low results / High behaviors): focus on role clarity, pairing, and accountability rhythm
  - Q3 (High results / Low behaviors): coaching on collaboration, cross-team impact; document expectations
  - Q4 (High results / High behaviors): candidate for stretch assignments & promotion discussion

Example short matrix entry (manager fill-in):
- Name: Jordan Patel | Results: Meets (=> moving to Exceeds) | Behaviors: Role-model | Current quadrant: Q4 | Evidence summary: shipped X feature with cross-team coordination; peer praise; mentored two new hires.

4) 30/60/90 and Probation Review Checklist
- Use for every new hire, internal transfer, or performance-improvement plan.
- Checkpoints: 30-day touch (engagement + training), 60-day progress (shipping/ownership evidence), 90-day outcome (role alignment and next steps).
- Probation template (to share with employee at start):
  - Objective: clear 3 measurable outcomes to achieve by day 90
  - Weekly owner: manager weekly 1:1 notes + shared progress doc
  - Failure criteria: not making measurable progress after documented support and two formal checkpoints -> escalate to People Ops for next steps

5) Promotion Readiness Evidence Pack (what managers should prepare)
- Required artifacts:
  - 1:1 notes (last 6–12 months) — bulletized highlights
  - Impact examples (3–5 clear examples with metrics where possible)
  - Stakeholder feedback (peers, partner engineering/product) — 1–3 short quotes
  - Growth areas and development plan if promoted
- Timeline: Nomination -> Manager packet due -> Calibration meeting (bi-weekly) -> Decision communicated within 10 business days.

6) Calibration Meeting Playbook
- Purpose: ensure consistent standards and defendable decisions across teams.
- Cadence: bi-weekly for engineering & product leadership; monthly for other orgs.
- Pre-reads (sent 48 hours before): manager packets (see above) and a one-slide summary per candidate.
- Meeting flow (30–45 minutes):
  1. Quick status (5 mins): number of cases, conflicts
  2. Candidate reviews (5–10 mins each): manager presents evidence, panel asks clarifying Qs
  3. Tone check & decision capture (10 mins): consensus + minority opinions recorded
  4. Action items (5 mins): Communicator, timeline, appeal route
- Decision rules: at least 60% of present calibrators must support promotion. If split, escalate to next-level manager + People Ops.

7) Documenting Difficult Conversations and Escalation Path
- For corrective coaching: create a short "Coaching Record" entry in the manager's notes with date, behavior, impact, request, and employee response.
- If improvement is not observed after 2 documented cycles (typically 8–12 weeks), escalate to People Ops with: coaching records, performance mapping, and suggested next steps.
- Escalation owners: People Ops lead (Priya Kapoor), HRBP for the org, and Partner Manager.

8) Onboarding Handoff & Early Development (first 60 days)
- Manager must provide within 3 days of start: role charter, initial OKRs, list of 3 people to introduce, and first 30/60/90 objectives.
- Week 1 checklist: access + 1:1 cadence set + buddy assigned + learning path link shared.
- Weeks 2–8: weekly manager 1:1 focused on context, deliverables, and integration into team rituals.

9) Templates (copyable)
- 1:1 note (one-line): "2027-02-01 | project: infra-opt | summary: removed blocker X, paired on Y | action: follow-up with ops (Michael) by 2027-02-07"
- Coaching note (short): "2027-01-15 | observation: missed SLA in Q4 deploy | impact: customer incident | request: write runbook and pair on next deploy by 2027-01-31"
- Promotion one-slide summary: "Name / Current role / Recommendation / Top 3 evidence bullets / Potential role after promotion / Ramp risks & plan"

10) Manager Training and Enablement
- People Ops runs quarterly workshops: "Effective 1:1s", "Giving Tough Feedback", and "Calibration Facilitation".
- New managers must attend a 2-hr onboarding workshop within 30 days of promotion to people manager.

11) Metrics and Reporting
- People Ops will track: 1) % of managers meeting 1:1 cadence, 2) % of hires with completed 90-day reviews, 3) distribution across performance quadrants, 4) time-to-decision for promotions.
- Monthly dashboard owner: People Ops Reporting (reporting@redwood-inference.internal) — includes anonymized counts and trends.

Appendix: Quick Reference Cheat Sheet
- Weekly 1:1s: 30 mins; Agenda = Check-in | Wins | Blockers | Development | Commitments
- Feedback framework: RAD (Recognize, Adjust, Develop)
- Promotion prep: 6–12 months of evidence, 3 impact examples, peer feedback
- Calibration rule: 60%+ support required or escalate
